messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: oncall-night for incident - 5xx spike and TLS handshake failures observed hitting api.redwood.com via Cloudflare edge in multiple regions. Please acknowledge and join #incidents.
oncall-night: acked. oncall-night here, joining.
sarah.k: I’m seeing 525/526 spikes in the frontend logs; clients getting TLS handshake failed from Cloudflare. Which regions are hit?
mike.chen: eu-west + us-east primarily. 5xx rate jumped ~18:34 UTC. Health checks for some endpoints also failing.
lee_ops: Confirming: Cloudflare edge is returning 525 for connections to api.redwood.com and some requests timing out. Origin health seems OK from our side.
anya_prod: Any impact to Dedicated or Private deployments? Customer SAs reporting some UI load failures.
james_support: A few customers on Hosted reported increased latency and request timeouts. No wide data loss but API errors increased.
oncall-night: Running quick dig/traceroute to see DNS path.
oncall-night: ```
$ dig +short api.redwood.com @8.8.8.8
104.21.34.12
172.67.21.9
``` 
oncall-night: traceroute shows packets stopping at Cloudflare edge hops in both regions.
observability-bot: Alert: 5xx-rate > 4% for /v1/generate across api-redwood-prod, triggered 18:35 UTC. Logs delayed from EU region (ingest backlog reported).
lee_ops: Observability vendor (ingest) is showing increased latency; some logs from EU are delayed ~2-4m. Might be blind spots.
sarah.k: Can someone check origin certs? Cloudflare 525 often means SSL handshake to origin failed.
mike.chen: Origin certs valid per certbot logs, not expiring. Also verified from our LB we can curl origin successfully: 200 OK.
anya_prod: Could be SNI mismatch or Cloudflare sending older TLS ciphers. Any recent Cloudflare settings changed?\nlee_ops: No recent config changes on our account. I’ll open CF support ticket. Meanwhile, mitigation ideas: bypass Cloudflare proxy for api.redwood.com (turn orange -> grey) to test direct traffic.
oncall-night: Propose temporary DNS override to origin A IP with low TTL to route clients direct, if CF proxy is failing. Need ops approval.
sarah.k: Approve. But watch firewall rules — we currently only allow Cloudflare IPs to origin. If we switch to direct, we must open origin to public or allow specific ranges.
mike.chen: We have origin pool with health checks on 443. I’ll add a temporary allow rule to LB for our egress region IPs and a small window for direct access. Rolling now.
james_support: Notifying affected customers: sending short banner on status page and support tickets for impacted tenants. ETA for update 10m.
observability-bot: Note: Datadog ingestion showing delayed logs; some traces from EU not processed yet. Alerts may be noisy.
lee_ops: Cloudflare ticket opened: #123456 - Customers reporting 525/526 SSL handshake failures at edge, agent assigned.
oncall-night: I’m toggling proxy off for api-redwood.com to test direct DNS (switching to grey cloud). Will do one edge at a time.
oncall-night: Switched staging subdomain to grey cloud — traffic to staging now direct and stable.
mike.chen: Good. Proceeding with prod fallback. Applying DNS A records with origin IPs and lower TTL (60s) while keeping cname for short time.
sarah.k: Firewall patched to allow direct connections from web. Watch for spikes, confirm no additional errors.
oncall-night: Prod DNS change live. Clients resolving to origin IPs, bypassing Cloudflare.
lee_ops: Early metrics: 5xx rate dropping, TLS handshake failures disappear from direct connections. Cloudflare still reporting edge errors.
anya_prod: Support update: customers seeing improvement. Status page updated.
james_support: Sending proactive customer email now. Note: Auth flows for some customers using SAML/Okta still intermittently affected — looks like session cookies timing out due to retries.
mike.chen: We should watch for abuse since origin is now public; re-enable tightened WAF rules and rate limits.
observability-bot: Logs from EU are catching up; some late-arriving traces show retries and backoff on client side increased 20%.
oncall-night: Reached Cloudflare support. They acknowledged an edge TLS regression in specific POPs and are rolling mitigations. They advise to keep proxy off until fixed.
lee_ops: Recommend keeping DNS direct for now and plan to revert after CF confirms fixed and we validate in canary.
sarah.k: Agree. Handoff: I’m going offline in ~20m. Leaving handoff notes: direct DNS active, firewall relaxed, WAF on, support notified, CF ticket #123456 open. If CF fixes, we test in canary then re-enable proxy.
oncall-night: Acknowledged. I’ll stay and monitor overnight. Oncall-night taking ownership for incident until 08:00 UTC handover.
anya_prod: Post-incident tasks: add runbook section for Cloudflare edge TLS failure, automate health-check rollback to direct origin, and create alert for Cloudflare SNI/525 pattern.
james_support: Drafting incident blurb for status.redwood.com: short summary + customer guidance + contact link.
observability-bot: Summary metrics: peak 5xx 6.1% at 18:36 UTC, dropped to 0.5% after DNS fallback at 18:42 UTC. Logs delayed by up to 5m.
oncall-night: Logging final timeline in the incident tracker and will create postmortem draft tomorrow. Marking incident as mitigated — monitoring in progress. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident updated: mitigated (partial) - DNS fallback to origin applied. Cloudflare ticket #123456 open. Next: postmortem and follow-up actions.
